q_en: What does the shape of a noun tell me before I know the word?
q_ar: مَاذَا يُخْبِرُنِي شَكْلُ الِاسْمِ قَبْلَ أَنْ أَعْرِفَ مَعْنَاهُ؟
not_yet: Every place, tool and little shape: only the common ones are here.
The feminine of “more” and the plurals of these nouns.
Belonging words that change their letters: look them up (Lesson 55).
not_yet_ar: كُلُّ أَوْزَانِ الْمَكَانِ وَالْأَدَاةِ وَالتَّصْغِيرِ: هُنَا الشَّائِعُ فَقَطْ.
نِسْبَةٌ تَتَغَيَّرُ حُرُوفُهَا: اُنْظُرْ فِي الْمُعْجَمِ (الدَّرْسُ ٥٥).

slides.head_en: Look: five jobs, each with its own shape
slides.head_ar: اُنْظُرْ: خَمْسُ وَظَائِفَ، وَلِكُلِّ وَظِيفَةٍ شَكْلٌ
sents: The boy opened the library door with the key.
A little boy sat among the men.
This is an Arabic book, and the teacher is from Tarim.
The mosque is bigger than the house.

lines: Every new word has a root you already know. Find the root of مَسْجِد · مِفْتَاح · وُلَيْد
لِكُلِّ كَلِمَةٍ جَدِيدَةٍ جَذْرٌ تَعْرِفُهُ. اِبْحَثْ عَنْهُ.
Which letters did the shape add to the root? Where: in front, in the middle, at the end?
أَيُّ حُرُوفٍ زَادَهَا الشَّكْلُ عَلَى الْجَذْرِ؟ فِي أَيِّ مَكَانٍ: فِي الْأَوَّلِ أَمْ فِي الْوَسَطِ أَمْ فِي الْآخِرِ؟
Look at the ending of أَكْبَرُ. Is there a tanwīn? Where have you seen that before?
اُنْظُرْ إِلَى آخِرِ «أَكْبَرُ». هَلْ فِيهِ تَنْوِينٌ؟ أَيْنَ رَأَيْتَ مِثْلَ ذَلِكَ؟

slides.head_en: Places and tools: the first letters tell you
slides.head_ar: الْمَكَانُ وَالْأَدَاةُ: أَوَّلُ الْكَلِمَةِ يَدُلُّ عَلَيْهِمَا

cards.def_ar: مَكَانُ الْفِعْلِ: مَـ ثُمَّ حُرُوفُ الْجَذْرِ.
cards.def_en: where the action happens: مَـ in front of the root

cards.def_ar: أَدَاةُ الْفِعْلِ: مِـ ثُمَّ حُرُوفُ الْجَذْرِ.
cards.def_en: what you use to do it: مِـ in front of the root
a small one, or a dear one
from, of, connected with: add ـِيّ to the noun
bigger, better, nearer … or the biggest. It takes no tanwīn.

slides.note: The shape tells you the job. The root tells you the idea.
slides.note_ar: الشَّكْلُ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الْوَظِيفَةِ، وَالْجَذْرُ يَدُلُّ عَلَى الْفِكْرَةِ.

slides.tip: It describes a noun, so it agrees with it: تَرِيمِيٌّ (m) · تَرِيمِيَّةٌ (f).
slides.tip_ar: هِيَ صِفَةٌ فَتُوَافِقُ الِاسْمَ: تَرِيمِيٌّ لِلْمُذَكَّرِ وَتَرِيمِيَّةٌ لِلْمُؤَنَّثِ.

slides.tip: مِنْ = “than”: الْمَسْجِدُ أَكْبَرُ مِنَ الْبَيْتِ. “The most”: أَكْبَرُ الْمَسَاجِدِ.
slides.tip_ar: «مِنْ» لِلْمُقَارَنَةِ. وَمَعَ الْجَمْعِ: أَكْبَرُ الْمَسَاجِدِ = الْأَكْبَرُ بَيْنَهَا.

slides.head_en: Try: what does the shape say?

slides.why: A student writes a tanwīn on أَكْبَر. Wrong! A “more” word takes no tanwīn (like أَحْمَد in Lesson 40): الْجَبَلُ أَكْبَرُ.
slides.why_ar: كَتَبَ طَالِبٌ تَنْوِينًا عَلَى «أَكْبَرٌ». هَذَا خَطَأٌ! الْكَلِمَةُ عَلَى وَزْنِ «أَفْعَل» لَا تَأْخُذُ تَنْوِينًا (مِثْلُ أَحْمَدَ فِي الدَّرْسِ ٤٠): الْجَبَلُ أَكْبَرُ.

can: I can tell from the shape of a noun that it names a place, a tool, a little one, belonging, or “more”.
I can find the root under the shape and use both to guess the meaning of a new word.
I can read a comparison with أَفْعَل … مِنْ and write the ending of “more” words correctly (no tanwīn).
can_ar: أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَعْرِفَ مِنْ شَكْلِ الِاسْمِ أَنَّهُ مَكَانٌ أَوْ أَدَاةٌ أَوْ تَصْغِيرٌ أَوْ نِسْبَةٌ أَوْ تَفْضِيلٌ.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَجِدَ الْجَذْرَ تَحْتَ الشَّكْلِ وَأَسْتَعْمِلَهُمَا فِي تَخْمِينِ مَعْنَى كَلِمَةٍ جَدِيدَةٍ.
أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ الْمُقَارَنَةَ «أَفْعَلُ مِنْ …» وَأَكْتُبَ آخِرَ كَلِمَةِ التَّفْضِيلِ كِتَابَةً صَحِيحَةً.

sections.name: A
sections.en: A real text: the mosques of Tarim. Read it aloud, then answer.
lines: وَأَشْهَرُ مَسَاجِدِ تَرِيمَ: مَسْجِدُ آلِ أَحْمَدَ، ...
The most famous mosques of Tarim: the mosque of Āl Aḥmad, ...
sections.source: Idām al-Qūt fī Dhikr Buldān Ḥaḍramawt (al-Saqqāf), the entry on Tarim
sections.cite: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. ʿUbayd Allāh b. Muḥsin al-Saqqāf, Idām al-Qūt fī Dhikr Buldān Ḥaḍramawt (Shamela copy 'Maʿjam buldān Ḥaḍramawt', SSD Master Library [173760]; printed edition not identified), p. 1/589 of the copy. The text is cut and the line about who first built the mosque is left out (the author himself notes a difference of view). TLNOOR 702 is a scan of the same work (not read for this entry). Course cut: only the first and the third clause are printed; the middle clause (on the renewal of the building) is left out and marked with “...”, so the two clauses are shown in the order of the source. Vowelled for learners (the consonants are the source’s).
sections.teacher_note: The two ★ rows are for adults. Children may skip them.

items.en: Translate line 1.
items.model: The most famous mosques of Tarim: the mosque of Āl Aḥmad, ...

items.en: Translate line 2.
What kind of text is this, and where is it from?
items.ar_q: أَيُّ نَوْعٍ مِنَ النُّصُوصِ هَذَا؟ وَمِنْ أَيْنَ هُوَ؟
items.model: A history of the towns of Ḥaḍramawt: Idām al-Qūt by al-Saqqāf, the entry on Tarim.

items.en: Which mosque does line 1 name?
items.model: The mosque of Āl Aḥmad (مَسْجِدُ آلِ أَحْمَدَ).

items.en: What does the mosque have, according to line 2? Which word means “many”?
items.ar_q: مَاذَا لِلْمَسْجِدِ فِي السَّطْرِ الثَّانِي؟ أَيُّ كَلِمَةٍ تَعْنِي «كَثِيرًا»؟

items.en: True or false?
items.model: False. The text speaks of “the most famous mosques” (many).
items.note: The text speaks of “the most famous mosques” (many).

items.en: Root hunt: find two words in the text built on the root س ج د. What does each name?
items.ar_q: ابْحَثْ عَنْ كَلِمَتَيْنِ جَذْرُهُمَا س ج د. عَلَى مَاذَا تَدُلُّ الْكَلِمَتَانِ؟
items.model: مَسَاجِدِ (mosques) and مَسْجِدُ (mosque): the place of prostrating.

items.en: ★ This word is on the “more” shape. Why is it not أَشْهَرٌ with tanwīn? What does the shape add to the idea “famous”?
items.ar_q: ★ لِمَاذَا لَيْسَتْ «أَشْهَرٌ» بِتَنْوِينٍ؟ مَاذَا يَزِيدُ الشَّكْلُ عَلَى مَعْنَى «شَهِير»؟
items.model: A “more” word takes no tanwīn (it ends in ـُ here). The shape adds “most”: the most famous.

items.en: ★ Why does تَرِيمَ end in ـَ although it follows “of” (the mosques of …)?
items.ar_q: ★ لِمَاذَا تَنْتَهِي «تَرِيمَ» بِفَتْحَةٍ مَعَ أَنَّهَا بَعْدَ «مَسَاجِدِ»؟
items.model: Tarim is a name that takes no tanwīn and no kasra (Lesson 40): it keeps ـَ.

sections.name: B
sections.en: A short text: in the mosque. Read it aloud, then answer.
lines: دَخَلَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ الْمَسْجِدَ الْكَبِيرَ فِي تَرِيمَ.
Ahmad entered the big mosque in Tarim with his father.
فِي الْمَسْجِدِ مِنْبَرٌ جَمِيلٌ وَمِحْرَابٌ قَدِيمٌ.
In the mosque there is a beautiful minbar and an old miḥrāb.
And at the entrance there is a big lamp.
جَلَسَ وُلَيْدٌ بَيْنَ الرِّجَالِ فِي الْحَلْقَةِ، وَكَانَ أَصْغَرَ الطُّلَّابِ.
A little boy sat among the men in the circle, and he was the youngest of the students.
وَكَانَ الْحَبِيبُ تَرِيمِيًّا، وَكَانَ أَعْلَمَ الرِّجَالِ فِي الْمَجْلِسِ.
The Habib was from Tarim, and he was the most knowledgeable of the men in the majlis.
ثُمَّ فَتَحَ أَبُو أَحْمَدَ بَابَ الْمَكْتَبَةِ بِالْمِفْتَاحِ.
Then Ahmad’s father opened the library door with the key.
وَقَالَ أَحْمَدُ: الْمَكْتَبَةُ أَكْبَرُ مِنَ الْمَدْرَسَةِ.
And Ahmad said: The library is bigger than the school.
And the Ḥaḍramī students read many books.
sections.teacher_note: The two ★ rows are for adults. Children may skip them.

items.ar_q: رَتِّبِ الْأَحْدَاثَ: (a) فَتَحَ الْأَبُ بَابَ الْمَكْتَبَةِ (b) دَخَلَ أَحْمَدُ الْمَسْجِدَ (c) قَالَ أَحْمَدُ إِنَّ الْمَكْتَبَةَ أَكْبَرُ.
options: Into the big mosque in Tarim.
A beautiful minbar and an old miḥrāb.

items.en: Root hunt: find three words built on the root ك ب ر. Which one means “more”?
items.ar_q: ابْحَثْ عَنْ ثَلَاثِ كَلِمَاتٍ جَذْرُهَا ك ب ر. أَيُّهَا تَعْنِي «أَكْثَر»؟

items.en: ★ In line 5, why does تَرِيمِيًّا end in ـًا, while الْحَضْرَمِيُّونَ in line 8 has the plural ending “-ūn”?
items.ar_q: ★ لِمَاذَا تَنْتَهِي «تَرِيمِيًّا» بِـ ـًا وَ«الْحَضْرَمِيُّونَ» بِـ ـُونَ؟
items.model: تَرِيمِيًّا is what is said about the Habib after كَانَ (ـًا). الْحَضْرَمِيُّونَ describes the doer (الطُّلَّابُ), so it takes the doer’s ending: the plural of people (“-ūn”).

items.en: ★ Why does أَصْغَرَ end in ـَ and not in tanwīn? (line 4)
items.model: A “more” word takes no tanwīn; and after كَانَ the thing said ends in ـَ.

sections.name: AA
sections.en: The Story Strip: lines 1–96
lines: A boy went to a mosque.
The boy sat in the mosque.
The boy opened a muṣḥaf (a copy of the Qur’an).
The boy read in the muṣḥaf.
The boy sat in the study circle.
The friends went to the mosque.
The students read in the books.
The Habib sat in the mosque.
The Habib is a righteous man.
Is the Habib in the mosque?
Yes, the Habib is in the mosque.
The boy came in through the door.
The mother looked at the boy.
The boy sits in the study circle today.
Maryam is reading the muṣḥaf now.
The boy was happy in the majlis.
Maryam was happy in the study circle.
The boy did not leave the majlis.
لَنْ يَجْلِسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْبَيْتِ غَدًا.
The boy will not sit at home tomorrow.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَبِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ.
The boy went with the father to the ziyāra (the visit).
The boy sat with good manners in the majlis.
The boy heard the Rātib (the litany) with his father.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ إِلَى بَيْتِ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy went in the morning to the Habib’s house.
The boy sat in the circle of dhikr (remembrance of Allah).
The Habib asked him about the lesson.
The boy served the guests and carried the food.
ثُمَّ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ وَسَمِعَ الدَّرْسَ.
Then the boy sat with the Habib and heard the lesson.
The guests thanked the boy who served them.
حَفِظَ الْوَلَدُ مَا سَمِعَ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy memorised what he heard from the Habib.
فَهِمَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ لِأَنَّهُ خَدَمَ الضُّيُوفَ.
The boy understood the lesson because he served the guests.
فِي الْمَجْلِسِ خَمْسَةُ ضُيُوفٍ وَسَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ كُلَّ كَلِمَةٍ.
There are five guests in the majlis, and the boy heard every word.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
The boy came to the ribāṭ in the morning.
The Habib said: Knowledge is light.
سَأَلَ عُمَرُ صَدِيقَهُ: هَلْ أَنْتَ ذَاهِبٌ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ؟
Umar asked his friend: Are you going to the rawḥa?
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: الصَّلَاةُ نُورٌ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Prayer is light.
The boy opened his muṣḥaf and read his wird (his daily portion).
صَلَّى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ ثُمَّ دَعَا.
The boy prayed with the students, then made duʿāʾ.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الْمَوْلِدَ لِأَنَّ مَحَبَّةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ فِي قَلْبِهِ.
The boy read the mawlid because love of the Prophet ﷺ is in his heart.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ لِأَبِي الْوَلَدِ: وَلَدُكَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ.
The Habib said to the boy’s father: Your son is a student of knowledge (ṭālib ʿilm).
جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي مَجَالِسِ الْعُلَمَاءِ فِي تَرِيمَ.
The boy sat in the gatherings of the scholars in Tarim.
يُقَالُ إِنَّ الْإِمَامَ وُلِدَ فِي تَرِيمَ.
It is said that the Imam was born in Tarim.
It was said to the boy: Knowledge is light.
عَلَّمَ الْحَبِيبُ الْوَلَدَ: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ.
The Habib taught the boy: O Allah, bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad ﷺ.
The boy reminded his friend of the prayer.
فِي اللَّيْلِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَصْحَابِ وَقَرَأَ الرَّاتِبَ.
At night the boy sat with the companions and read the Rātib.
قَالُوا: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ.
They said: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and Allah is greater.
فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ مَعَ أَبِيهِ.
On the Night of Qadr the boy sat in the mosque with his father.
The boy helped the guests and honoured them.
The students helped one another in the ribāṭ.
The boy was humble and learned from them.
اِنْتَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ الْحَبِيبَ عِنْدَ بَابِ الْمَسْجِدِ.
The boy waited for the Habib at the door of the mosque.
اِجْتَمَعَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ وَاسْتَمَعَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْحَبِيبِ.
The students gathered in the morning and the boy listened to the Habib.
حَجَّ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ مِنْ مَكَّةَ.
The boy’s father made the pilgrimage, then returned from Mecca.
أَخَذَ الْوَلَدُ التَّمْرَ مِنْ أَبِيهِ وَقَدَّمَهُ لِلضُّيُوفِ.
The boy took the dates from his father and offered them to the guests.
The boy heard a ḥadīth with its chain.
قَالَ الرَّاوِي: حَدَّثَنَا وَأَخْبَرَنَا، ثُمَّ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ.
The narrator said: He told us, and he informed us, then the Prophet ﷺ said: Deeds are only by intentions.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: قُلْ آمَنْتُ بِاللَّهِ فَاسْتَقِمْ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Say: I believe in Allah, and then be upright.
The boy stood up and said: I believe in Allah.
مَشَى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ وَوَصَلَ فِي الْمَسَاءِ.
The boy walked with his father to the ziyāra and arrived in the evening.
The boy made duʿāʾ: O Allah, guide us.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَقَالَ: مَا أَحْسَنَ هَذَا الْمَجْلِسَ!
The boy came to the majlis and said: How beautiful this majlis is!
قَالَ لِأُمِّهِ: جِئْتُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَرَأَيْتُ الْحَبِيبَ.
He said to his mother: I came to the majlis and I saw the Habib.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ كَلِمَاتٍ مِنْ جَذْرٍ وَاحِدٍ: عَلَّمَ، مُعَلِّمٌ، تَعْلِيمٌ.
The boy wrote words from one root: ʿallama, muʿallim, taʿlīm.
And he wrote: sāfara, musāfir, safar.
نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى مِنْبَرِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَمِحْرَابِهِ.
The boy looked at the minbar of the mosque and its miḥrāb.
قَالَ الْوَلَدُ: أَنَا حَضْرَمِيٌّ مِنْ تَرِيمَ.
The boy said: I am a Ḥaḍramī, from Tarim.

items.model: The boy looked at the minbar of the mosque and its miḥrāb. The boy said: I am a Ḥaḍramī, from Tarim.

items.model: مِنْبَر: the pulpit; مِحْرَاب: the prayer niche. Their shape (مِـ in front) often names a tool or a place.

Write in Arabic: I am from Tarim.
